advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile `_foreign_store_paths` classification with `_ticket_dirs` so an empty/CREATE-less ticket directory is not both MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:421-429 `_holds_events` returns True only when `any(n.endswith('.json') or n.endswith(RETIRED_SUFFIX) ... if not n.startswith('.'))`
fsck_repair.py:100-107 `_ticket_dirs` returns every `d` where `not d.startswith('.') and os.path.isdir(...)` — no event-file requirement
src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:123-124 an empty/CREATE-less ticket dir is already surfaced as `MISSING_CREATE` by check 2
docstring at fsck.py:412-415 asserts parity: 'it uses the same is this a ticket? test as the rest of fsck'
advisory.finding: `_foreign_store_paths` claims to use 'the same is-this-a-ticket test as the rest of fsck', but its `_holds_events` test (requires >=1 immediate non-dot `.json`/`.retired` file) is stricter than `_ticket_dirs` (treats ANY non-dot directory as a ticket). An empty ticket directory, or one whose remaining event files are all dot-prefixed, is a ticket for checks 2/4/5 (reported MISSING_CREATE) yet is flagged as a FOREIGN_STORE_PATH stray here — a false positive and a double-report of the same directory.
scenarios: A ticket directory with no CREATE event yet (or all events retired to dotfiles) exists at tracker top level
fsck runs and both MISSING_CREATE and FOREIGN_STORE_PATH fire for the same directory, inflating issue_count and mislabeling store data as source pollution
advisory.suggested_fix: Treat any non-dot directory as ticket data (mirror `_ticket_dirs`, letting check 2 own the empty/missing-CREATE case), or explicitly restrict FOREIGN_STORE_PATH to non-directory top-level entries and directories that hold non-event content; document the intended divergence if deliberate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that commits a foreign top-level path into the tickets branch and asserts the report names it as COMMITTED (not 'None are committed').
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:440-447: committed = [n for n in strays if not path_is_foreign_to_branch(tracker, n)] … f" {len(committed)} of them are COMMITTED to the tickets branch …"

All four tests exercise only the else branch: test_source_tree_in_the_tracker_is_reported asserts `"None are committed" in report` (line 44); no test commits a foreign path so `committed` is always empty.
Commit message: 'separately names any stray the branch actually TRACKS -- those were committed and will propagate on the next push, which is strictly worse than a working-tree stray.'

src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:421-429: `_holds_events` does `os.listdir(path)` inside a try/except OSError; a regular file path raises NotADirectoryError (an OSError subclass) → returns False → treated as a stray.
All strays in the tests are directories (src/, tests/, human-readable-ticket-name); no top-level plain file is placed in the tracker.
advisory.finding: The COMMITTED-to-branch reporting branch of _foreign_store_paths is untested: no test creates a stray that path_is_foreign_to_branch treats as tracked, so the 'N of them are COMMITTED to the tickets branch … and will propagate on the next push' report path never runs. This is the strictly-worse case the change explicitly adds and the commit message centers on.
merged_from: No test covers a top-level FILE stray (as opposed to a directory) in the tracker. _holds_events relies on os.listdir raising OSError for a non-directory to classify a plain file as a stray; this edge is exercised by no test.
scenarios: A raw `git add`/`git commit` of a src/ path into the tickets branch — the exact scenario the check is designed to surface as the more severe case.
A regression inverting the committed/foreign classification or breaking the 'COMMITTED' detail string would pass all existing tests.
